solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Hash in bowl on floor? (4,9)

blocks.note: not food here: a hash is a botched job, a mess
taken literally: a pet's morning meal, served on the floor

annotation.surface: Someone describes where the hash has ended up: in a bowl on the floor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hash' looks like food, which the second half keeps up; it is really the British slang sense of a botched job, which is what 'a dog's breakfast' means.
annotation.definitionFit: To make a hash of something is to make a mess of it, and a dog's breakfast is a complete mess.

entries.clue: Given instigation of divorce, could the answer be — this? (11)

annotation.definition: Given instigation of divorce, could the answer be — this?

indicatorNotes.instigation of: the instigation is the start, so take the first letter

blocks.note: turned into a statement: 'the answer is SOLUTION'

annotation.surface: A question about what follows once a divorce has been set in motion.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: D followed by IS SOLUTION, and the dissolution of a marriage is exactly what a divorce brings about.
annotation.definitionFit: Dissolution is the formal ending of a marriage, which is what a divorce is.

entries.clue: I moved earth toward heaven to inspire Barcelona, ultimately — did I? (5)

annotation.definition: I moved earth toward heaven to inspire Barcelona, ultimately — did I?

indicatorNotes.toward heaven: in a down entry, going up toward heaven means reading from the bottom
indicatorNotes.to inspire: to inspire is to breathe in, so the letters take something inside
indicatorNotes.ultimately: ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter of Barcelona counts

blocks.note: I DUG: dug is moved earth

annotation.surface: A voice asks whether it really shifted earth skyward to fire up Barcelona.
annotation.walkthrough: I DUG turned upward gives GUDI, which takes in A. The whole clue is also the definition: Gaudí dug the foundations of the Sagrada Família, rising toward heaven, in Barcelona.
annotation.definitionFit: Antoni Gaudí is the architect whose soaring buildings, above all the Sagrada Família, define Barcelona.

entries.clue: Beat this good French Olympian spirit (5,4)

blocks.note: the Olympians were the gods of Mount Olympus

annotation.surface: A challenge to top the fine French Olympic spirit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Beat this' reads as a boast; it is the definition, a thing you beat. 'Olympian' suggests an athlete, but here it is a god of Mount Olympus.
annotation.definitionFit: A bongo drum is played by beating it with the hands.

entries.clue: European river in Piedmont city almost bordering a kingdom of Italy (7)

indicatorNotes.in: the river goes inside the city
indicatorNotes.almost: the city loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.bordering: a country bordering another sits right beside it, so A is placed directly after the city

blocks.note: TURIN, the capital of Piedmont, without its last letter

annotation.surface: A travel note about a European river passing near a Piedmont city.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a modern tourist route; the answer is ancient history, and 'kingdom' is the only word hinting at it.
annotation.definitionFit: Etruria was the ancient Etruscan kingdom in what is now Tuscany.

entries.clue: Imperative in conference to make a bloomer, say? (5)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition describes what you do to make a loaf: knead is the verb

indicatorNotes.in conference: conferring is talking, so the word is heard, not seen

blocks.note: a need is an imperative, something you must have

annotation.surface: A meeting rule that insists someone commit a blunder.
annotation.walkthrough: A bloomer looks like a blunder; here it is a long British loaf of white bread with a rounded top, and dough for it must be kneaded.
annotation.definitionFit: Kneading the dough is how you make a loaf such as a bloomer.

entries.clue: Lamenting being in a muddle — what might set one straight? (9)

indicatorNotes.in a muddle: something in a muddle is disordered, so the letters of lamenting come out of order

annotation.surface: Someone grieving in confusion looks for something to put them right.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Set one straight' sounds like advice to a troubled person; alignment literally sets things in a straight line.
annotation.definitionFit: Alignment is the arrangement that puts things straight, in line.

entries.clue: Brown belt (3)

blocks.note: a colour: a light yellowish brown, as of leather
a verb: to thrash, as in giving someone a hiding

annotation.surface: A brown belt, the martial-arts grade.
annotation.walkthrough: The pair read as a single judo rank; split them and 'belt' is a verb meaning hit.
annotation.definitionFit: Tan is a light yellowish brown, and to tan also means to thrash.

entries.clue: Biblical character James authorises arrests (4)

indicatorNotes.arrests: the phrase holds the answer captive inside it

annotation.surface: A man named James signs off on some arrests.
annotation.walkthrough: James sounds like the apostle, making the answer seem to be another New Testament name; Esau is Jacob's twin from Genesis.
annotation.definitionFit: Esau, elder twin of Jacob, sold his birthright in Genesis.

entries.clue: European region, 75 per cent in want, unfortunately (9)

indicatorNotes.75 per cent: keep three of the four letters of want
indicatorNotes.unfortunately: things going badly suggests the letters are mixed up

annotation.surface: A report that three quarters of some European region is sadly poor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'European region' reads as one phrase; 'European' alone is the definition and 'region' is part of the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: a person from Norway is one kind of European.

entries.clue: Big rock in castle rolled back, charger not initially gaining access (3-1-4)

indicatorNotes.not initially: the word is missing at the start, so its first letter is dropped
indicatorNotes.gaining access: the charger gets inside the castle

blocks.note: in chess the castle is also called the rook
RHINO, famous for charging, loses its R

annotation.surface: A boulder in a castle gets rolled back while a warhorse struggles to get in.
annotation.walkthrough: The charger is not a horse but a rhino. 'Big rock' sounds like a boulder; it is the famous diamond in the British Crown Jewels.
annotation.definitionFit: The Koh-i-Noor is one of the largest cut diamonds in the world, a very big rock.

entries.clue: Hard in dark for rescuer at sea? (6)

indicatorNotes.in: H goes inside the other word

annotation.surface: Something hard to find in the dark that will save someone at sea.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a dinghy is only one example of a sea rescuer, such as a lifeboat's inflatable tender.
annotation.definitionFit: A dinghy is a small boat, often used to pick people up from the water.

entries.clue: Party girls embracing OAP, I’m so embarrassed man! (4,7)

indicatorNotes.embracing: the party girls wrap around the other letters
indicatorNotes.embarrassed: flustered, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the women at a hen party, a British bachelorette party
anagram fodder, 7 letters; an OAP is a British old-age pensioner

annotation.surface: A pensioner caught up at a hen party blushes and cries out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Man!' reads as an exclamation of embarrassment; it is the definition, mankind as a species.
annotation.definitionFit: Homo sapiens is the scientific name for the human species, man.

entries.clue: Unstoppable force in prison, criminal anger, note (10)

indicatorNotes.criminal: wrong, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: ut is the old name for the note do

annotation.surface: A dangerous inmate's rage is described as an unstoppable force.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' seems to belong with prison; it is the instruction to mix up ANGER.
annotation.definitionFit: A juggernaut is a huge, overwhelming force that crushes whatever is in its path.

entries.clue: Adhesive with which I stick a vessel up on top of cupboard (3,6)

indicatorNotes.up: in a down entry, reading upward reverses the letters
indicatorNotes.on top of: in a down entry, this chunk sits above the next
indicatorNotes.top of: the top of a down-standing word is its first letter, so cupboard gives just C

annotation.surface: Instructions for gluing a jug to the top of a cupboard.
annotation.walkthrough: The reversed chunk comes first and I tucks in above C at the foot.
annotation.definitionFit: Gum arabic is a natural gum from acacia trees, used as a glue.

entries.clue: Very fast twitch has hurried boy through (9)

indicatorNotes.through: the hurried boy passes through the middle of the twitch

annotation.surface: A lad dashes through so fast he seems to twitch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Very fast twitch' reads like muscle fibre jargon, but the definition ends at 'fast'.
annotation.definitionFit: Transonic describes speeds close to the speed of sound, which is very fast.

entries.clue: Graduate on cover of exam book (4)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across entry, the graduate comes after
indicatorNotes.cover of: the cover is the outside, so take the outer letters

annotation.surface: A graduate's name printed on the cover of an exam booklet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Exam book' reads as one thing; 'book' is the definition, Jane Austen's novel.
annotation.definitionFit: Emma is a novel by Jane Austen.

entries.clue: Concern for international relations, maybe, all kicking off (4)

indicatorNotes.kicking off: starting, so take the first letter of each word

annotation.surface: A worry about foreign affairs, with everyone starting to fight.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Concern' reads as a worry; it is a business, as in 'a going concern'. 'All' tells you every word gives a letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Concern in its commercial sense, as in 'a going concern', is a plain synonym for a business.

entries.clue: Listener redundant in the end after I’m introduced to film — silent movie star? (4,6)

indicatorNotes.in the end: what comes in the end of redundant is its final letter
indicatorNotes.after: the listener and the end letter follow I'M
indicatorNotes.introduced to: the whole chunk is put inside the film

blocks.note: a film of mist on glass

annotation.surface: A cinema story: a sound man is laid off once a silent star joins the picture.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Film' makes you think of movies; here it is a thin layer, MIST, which opens after M to take in IMEART.
annotation.definitionFit: A mime artist performs without speaking, so is a star of silent movement.

entries.clue: Alcoholic drink with guile secreted in pocket (7)

indicatorNotes.secreted in: to secrete something is to hide it away, so guile goes inside pocket

blocks.note: pocket as an adjective, pocket-sized: mini

annotation.surface: A drink cunningly smuggled in a pocket.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pocket' reads as a noun you hide things in; it is an adjective meaning small, as in a pocket calculator.
annotation.definitionFit: A martini is a cocktail of gin or vodka with vermouth.

entries.clue: Open University hit by opponents (6)

blocks.note: North and West, partners at bridge, are the opponents of South and East
a rap is a sharp hit

annotation.surface: The Open University is struck by its rivals.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Open University' is a British distance-learning institution, so the pair looks inseparable; 'Open' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: taking the paper off a present opens it.

entries.clue: Gallery’s bill for frames (5)

indicatorNotes.frames: one word surrounds the other like a picture frame

blocks.note: a bill is a poster, an advertisement

annotation.surface: An art gallery's invoice for picture frames.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Frames' fits the gallery picture as a noun; it is the verb telling PRO to surround AD.
annotation.definitionFit: The Prado is the national art gallery in Madrid.

entries.clue: Credit claimed by priest for amending decree (8)

indicatorNotes.claimed by: taken up by, so the credit joins the priest's letters
indicatorNotes.amending: changing, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A priest takes the credit for changing an order.
annotation.walkthrough: A rescript is an old word for an official edict, especially a papal or imperial reply, so a priest suits the picture.
annotation.definitionFit: A formal, rather archaic synonym: historically an emperor's or pope's written ruling in answer to a query.

entries.clue: Gallant, first person donning jumper (5)

indicatorNotes.donning: putting on, so the jumper wraps round the first person

blocks.note: a roo, a kangaroo, is a jumper
me is the first person pronoun

annotation.surface: A dashing man pulls on a sweater first.
annotation.walkthrough: A jumper is British for a sweater, which suits 'donning'; here it is an animal that jumps.
annotation.definitionFit: A gallant is a ladies' man, and a Romeo is an ardent lover.

entries.clue: Card issuer printed banking instruction firstly: sign alongside it (9)

indicatorNotes.banking: a bank lines each side of a river, so RAN sits either side of I
indicatorNotes.firstly: firstly means at the start, so only the opening letter of instruction is used
indicatorNotes.alongside: the sign sits next to the rest

blocks.note: Libra is a sign of the zodiac
a newspaper ran the story: printed it

annotation.surface: A bank card printed with an instruction and a place to sign.
annotation.walkthrough: The banking talk points to a credit card; the card is a library card. RAN splits after R to take in I.
annotation.definitionFit: A librarian issues library cards to borrowers.

entries.clue: European doffs cap for John (3)

indicatorNotes.doffs cap: removing the cap takes off the top letter

blocks.note: a Slav is a European; drop the S

annotation.surface: A European raises his hat to a man called John.
annotation.walkthrough: 'John' is not a name here but American slang for a toilet, and a lav (lavatory) is the British word.
annotation.definitionFit: A john and a lav are both informal words for a toilet.

entries.clue: Gather I’m from another planet! (4)

blocks.note: I am: the speaker is ME

annotation.surface: An alien announces itself on arrival.
annotation.walkthrough: The exclamation is the whole wordplay: 'I'm an alien' becomes ME, ET.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the intransitive verb: people assembling in one place.

entries.clue: Award gold medallist the first clue? (8,5)

blocks.note: the gold medal goes to the winner, the victor
the first clue in a crossword is 1 across, with I as the Roman one

annotation.surface: A prize for the winner of the very first clue.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue talks about the crossword itself: this puzzle's first clue is literally 1 across.
annotation.definitionFit: The Victoria Cross is Britain's highest award for gallantry in battle.
